messages:
alex_dev: Heads up — support ticket #4721: customer on v1.3.0 TS SDK started getting 401s after our CI regenerated clients yesterday. Anyone else see this?

ci-bot: deploy-bot: regen job completed for openapi@2025-03-14T03:12Z — artifacts published: clients/python, clients/ts, clients/go (job id: regen-8f3a2d)

maria_sdk: Hmm, did the OpenAPI spec change around security definitions? A rework in the spec could change the generator output. Can you paste a minimal request/response from the customer logs?

alex_dev: From customer logs: `GET /v1/models` => 401. Response snippet: `{"error":"unauthorized"}`. Response headers show `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="Redwood"`. They say their code still sets an auth token. Example from their app: 

```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models
```

sam_ci: I did a quick bisect locally. The regenerate commit 8f3a2d bumped the TS generator tool to @openapi/cli v0.12. That version changed the auth header wiring in the fetch wrapper — it now emits an `auth` header name instead of `authorization` in some code paths.

chen_oncall: :grimacing: If the header name changed to `auth`, proxies that expect `Authorization` would reject it. Can you paste the generated snippet showing the header key?

alex_dev: Sure. Old client (working):

```ts
headers['authorization'] = `Bearer ${token}`
```

New generated client (broken):

```ts
headers['auth'] = `Bearer ${token}`
```

maria_sdk: OK. That's the root cause. Generator rename likely came from a mapping in the security schemes -> header param. We'll need a 2-step fix: (1) patch the TS client to accept both `auth` and `authorization` (prefer `authorization`), publish a patch release; (2) pin the regen ci tool to v0.11 until we validate generator changes and update changelog. I'll open a PR.

sam_ci: Also add a small e2e to regen CI that runs a request against our auth-proxy docker image to ensure `Authorization` header is present. And add a changelog entry so customers know about any generator-influenced surface changes.

alex_dev: I'll reply to the customer with repro steps and a temporary workaround: manually add `headers['authorization'] = headers['auth'] || headers['authorization']` before performing requests, or use the canary once published. Will mention ETA for patch.

maria_sdk: Working on the PR now. ETA ~2h for a patch and canary. Changes: map both header names in runtime, add test, update generator mapping docs.

ci-bot: CI: created canary package ts-sdk@1.3.1-canary.1 — artifact: https://ci.internal.redwood/artefacts/regen/ts-sdk/1.3.1-canary.1

chen_oncall: :thumbsup: Thanks — please also add a short monitoring rule: alert on 401 spikes for /v1/* endpoints in the hour after regen runs. We should catch regressions earlier.

alex_dev: Will draft the alert and ping #support with a templated customer response.

maria_sdk: P.S. I'll also add an automation: regen job will run a smoke test that includes validating header names against a small contract. That should prevent silent surface regressions.
